name: Hidden Falls (pls read event details)
description:
HIDDEN FALLS - SUNDAY 26 July (full day)
REGISTRATION WITH THE WALK LEADER IS ESSENTIAL

RATED: Hard
There is no track and the route is a long rock hop over rocks and boulders (some slippery), followed by a steep climb and a bushbash near the end.  Return will be via the same route.

Good stamina and balance for creek rock hopping and boulder scrambling is required.

Numbers have to be restricted due to the small space available at the waterfall.

WHAT TO BRING:
- Water: enough for a full day or refill from the creek. We recommend water is treated before consumption.
- Clothing and gear: full long sleeve clothing is recommended. Many members also wear fingerless gloves. 
- Footwear: enclosed footwear
- Hat and sunprotection
- Personal first aid kit including insect repellent, compression bandage and blister kit.
- Swimming gear: there will be opportunity to swim at the lunch pool and on the way home

COST: Non-members $5 walk fee
Must be over 18years to participate

MEET:
7:30am on the Bruce Hwy opposite Alligator Creek Roadhouse
Aim to be back at the cars by 5pm
 
REGISTRATION and MORE INFO:
To discuss suitability, registration or for more info please contact the walk leader (Keith) or email tsvbush@hotmail.com and we will get back to you asap.

Please note:
 To protect the privacy of club officials, walk leaders, property owners or sensitive areas, contact details and some locations won't be published on Facebook or website. Please contact the club via email and we will respond ASAP. 
 
 On some activities, walker numbers may be limited to promote the safety and enjoyment of all, due to location size and ability to socially distance or to reduce our environmental impact at some locations.
 
 COVID-19
 Please do not attend if you are unwell, have symptoms or have been ordered to quarantine or isolate. Social distancing and self managed hygiene practices are strongly encouraged, and the club will not be organising car pooling opportunities at present. The club is cognisant of the QORF COVID SAFE PLAN for Outdoor Recreation Providers. On some walks, as noted above, numbers may be limited.
 
 We hope to see you on a walk soon.

name: Mt Storth (pls read event description)
description:
SUNDAY 19th July - Mt Storth (full day)

REGISTRATION WITH THE WALK LEADER IS ESSENTIAL. PLEASE READ THE INFORMATION BELOW.

RATED - Hard
Approx. 9hrs bushwalking. There is a long steep hill climb, no track, long grass, uneven footings, scrub, with return home via a creek rock hop.

DESCRIPTION
Mt Storth is the northern summit of the Mt Elliot range of Bowling Green Bay National Park (north of Alligator Ck). It is 632m altitude. To summit, it is a steep climb up a long spur without a track.  Whilst scrubby at the lower reaches, the vegetation changes as we climb towards the summit. Lunch will be at the summit and depending on what time we get there, there are two ways we could descend. The most likely is via Killymoon Creek (a good rock hop, boulder scramble and nice cascades) or if time is short we'll go down Dribble Creek (rock hop, boulder scramble also but shorter).

The walk commences and traverses private property and then enters the national park.

FITNESS
To be suitable for this walk, a good analogy would be doing a Castle Hill spur, without a track, three times with ease before lunchtime.

WHAT TO BRING
- Water: you will need water for full day eg minimum 4L
- Clothing: there is a lot of long grass and scrub so full long sleeve clothing is recommended. Many members also wear fingerless gloves.
- Enclosed footwear
- Food for the day
- Hat, sunscreen and insect repellent
- Usual bushwalking gear 
- Personal first aid kit including a compression bandage and blister kit is recommended.
- Swimming gear (if we come down Killymoon there may be opportunity for a swim at the main pool)

COST
Non members = $5 walk fee for insurance
Must be over 18years to participate

WALK LEADER, INFO and REGISTRATION
Walk leader is Wilfred
To discuss suitability, to register or for more information please contact tsvbush@hotmail.com and we will get back to you asap. 

WALK DETAILS
Meet time: 0700 for a 0715 departure at Alligator Ck (address will be given upon registration)
Return time: Aim to be back at the cars at 1700-1800 (but don't plan a dinner date!)

Please note:
To protect the privacy of club officials, walk leaders, property owners or sensitive areas, contact details and some locations won't be published on Facebook or website. Please contact the club via email and we will respond ASAP. 

On some activities, walker numbers may be limited to promote the safety and enjoyment of all, due to location size and ability to socially distance or to reduce our environmental impact at some locations.

COVID-19

Social distancing and self managed hygiene practices are strongly encouraged, and the club will not be organising car pooling opportunities at present. The club is cognisant of the QORF COVID SAFE PLAN for Outdoor Recreation Providers. On some walks, as noted above, numbers may be limited.

name: FULL - Dalrymple Gap Walking Track (pls read event description)
description:
Registrations for this walk have closed as walk capacity has been reached. 

SATURDAY 18th July  – Dalrymple Gap track 16 km. Full day.

RATED – EASY . National Park track walk with creek crossings and a hill.
REGISTRATION WITH THE WALK LEADER IS ESSENTIAL.
PLEASE READ ALL OF THE INFORMATION BELOW.

It's a great time of year to walk the Dalrymple Gap track. The creek is still flowing and temperatures are not too hot. This walk will be an out and back walk from the southern access point to the old bridge return.

A detailed walk description and history is on the QLD Govt Parks and Forests website. https://parks.des.qld.gov.au/parks/dalrymple-gap/about
This historic route is a nice 8km rainforest  track walk from southern end following the creek, then up a hill to the historic old stone bridge at top of range. There are several creek crossings and if there is water above rocks will have to wade (last Saturday the rocks were under water at first crossing). At the bridge, we turn around and return by same route. There is an opportunity for a swim at a pool.

To comfortably enjoy this walk you should be able to complete Castle Hill and be confident with the distance.

WHEN – Sunday 18th July

0830 Meet at walk start Southern Access point (Ingham  end, near Broadwater). The last five kilometres of road is unsealed, but can be accessed using a conventional vehicle. Driving directions at this link (allow 2 hrs drive) :

https://parks.des.qld.gov.au/parks/dalrymple-gap/visiting-safely

If you wish to follow Keith (walk leader) from Ingham, meet at McDonalds Ingham at 0745.

We should be back at the cars by 1600. Then 2 hr drive home.

WHAT TO BRING:

Bring snacks / food for morning tea and lunch.

Water – carry drinking water for 1 day walking – at a minimum 2 lt water and refill from creek as required (treat the water). 

Clothing – recommend long sleeve clothing. Small day pack. Hat, sunscreen, insect repellent. 

Footwear – enclosed footwear suitable for rock hopping / bushwalking. Swimming costume or similar for the pool swim.

First Aid kit - we recommend you carry a small personal first aid kit including a compression bandage and blister treatment supplies.

COST:
Non-members $5 walk fee.

Must be 18yrs or over to participate.

REGISTRATION OR MORE INFO:

Please email the club tsvbush@hotmail.com for walk leader (Keith) contact details. For the the privacy of walk leaders, contact details and some locations won’t be published on Facebook.

Walker numbers will be limited to promote the safety and enjoyment of all and to reduce our environmental impact. 

Due to COVID-19, please do not attend if you are unwell. Social distancing and hygiene practices are strongly encouraged.

name: Killymoon Crk - Introductory walk (FULL)
description:
Please note registrations have closed as the walk capacity has been reached.

12 July 2020 - Killymoon Creek (Allligator Creek area).
Please read all of the information below. Registration is essential - see below for details. Thanks.

KILLYMOON CREEK is an ideal half-day walk for an introduction to creek based bushwalking.

It's a great time of year to try Killymoon as it will be flowing but easily walkable. It's a pretty creek with small cascades along the creek and a good pool at the turn around point.

WHAT THE WALK INVOLVES: 
We'll be walking up a creek with rockhopping, boulder scrambling, and traversing rock ledges alongside cascades. The walk to the creek is part track, with a hill to cross.

MEETING TIME + DUARTION:
Meet time 0800 at Alligator Creek (exact location will be given when you register for the walk as it's a private residence).
We should be back at the cars around 1300, but don’t plan anything until much later.

WHAT TO BRING:
Bring snacks / food for morning tea at the creek pool. If you're someone who gets hungry perhaps bring an extra snack incase we're late returning.

Water – carry drinking water for ½ day walking – at a minimum 2 lt water and refill from creek as required (treat the water).

Clothing – recommend long sleeve clothing. Small day pack. Hat, sunscreen and insect repellent.

Footwear – enclosed footwear suitable for rock hopping / bushwalking. Swimming costume or similar for the pool swim.

A basic first aid kit including a snake bandage and blister kit are recommended.

COST:
Non-members $5 fee (for insurance cover)

FOR MORE INFO or TO REGISTER:
If you have any questions or wish to register please email the club tsvbush@hotmail.com.

(To maintain privacy for walk leaders we don't publish contact details. Thanks for your understanding)

All walkers must be 18+ years for insurance purposes.
Members welcome also.

Walk numbers will be limited to ensure everyone's enjoyment and safety. COVID safe guidelines will be followed. Please do not attend if you are unwell.

See you on the trails soon.
